title: Indian Nationals Among 14 Killed in Fujairah Multi-Vehicle Crash and Fire
excerpt: A truck lost control shortly before midnight on Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Road, overturned and caught fire in a 23-vehicle pile-up; India's consulate in Dubai says it has reached out to bereaved families.
body:
• Fourteen people were killed and 30 injured in a pile-up involving 23 vehicles, 18 cars and five trucks, on Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Road at the entrance to Fujairah, after a truck lost control, overturned and caught fire.
  • Fifteen of the 30 injured have been discharged from hospital and 15 remain hospitalised, Fujairah Police said.
  • The Consulate General of India in Dubai confirmed Indian nationals were among those killed and said it has reached out to bereaved families; the exact number of Indian nationals killed has not been disclosed.
  • Readers should rely only on official Fujairah Police channels for updates: the UAE Ministry of Interior urged the public not to circulate rumours or unverified information, and DNA testing is under way to identify some victims.

Indian nationals were among 14 people killed in a multi-vehicle crash in Fujairah, in the United Arab Emirates, after a truck lost control shortly before midnight on Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Road, at the entrance to the emirate, authorities said. Thirty other people were injured.

According to Fujairah Police, in an updated statement shared by the UAE Ministry of Interior on Thursday, November 12 and reported by Gulf Business, the truck initially collided with another vehicle before overturning and striking several vehicles that had stopped because of slow-moving traffic. The collision caused the truck to catch fire, with flames spreading to several other damaged vehicles. In total, 23 vehicles were involved: 18 cars and five trucks.

"Deeply saddened by the tragic road accident in Fujairah that claimed lives of several people, including Indian nationals. The Consulate has reached out to the bereaved families and is closely working with local authorities to provide all possible assistance and support."

That statement, from the Consulate General of India in Dubai on its official X account, is the confirmation that Indian nationals are among the dead. Gulf Business reported that the exact number of Indian nationals killed in the accident has not been disclosed, and authorities have not yet provided a complete breakdown of the nationalities of those who died.

The Indian victims, as reported so far

Reports from Kerala identified three members of a family from Malappuram among those who died, according to Fact.net.in: 21-year-old twins Muhammed Asmil and Misna Jubin, and Misna's three-year-old son, Muhammed Fayis. The same report said other family members were also injured in the collision. Those names are reported here as that source stated them; officials have not released a complete list of the deceased, and police confirmed that the identities of several victims are still being established through DNA testing.

Police confirmed that the deceased included Emirati nationals. The injured include nationals from the UAE, Oman, India, Brazil, Pakistan, Jordan and Egypt, according to Fujairah Police. Of the 30 people injured, 15 had been discharged from hospital after receiving treatment by Thursday, while the remaining 15 continued to receive medical care, depending on the severity of their injuries.

Response and investigation

Fujairah Police said its operations room received a report of the accident, prompting an immediate response from specialised police teams, ambulance and rescue personnel, and civil defence. Emergency teams worked to extinguish the fire, provide medical assistance to the injured and transport victims to hospitals, while authorities secured the accident site and managed traffic.

The UAE Ministry of Interior confirmed that Fujairah Police General Headquarters, in coordination with the relevant authorities, continues to handle the incident and investigate its circumstances in accordance with established procedures, and that the relevant authorities are continuing the legal and technical procedures related to the accident. Fujairah Police expressed sorrow over the accident, extended condolences to the families of those who died and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

What officials are asking the public to do

The Ministry of Interior stressed that information about the accident should be obtained exclusively through official Fujairah Police channels, which will provide further updates as they become available, and urged residents to refrain from sharing unverified information while investigations remain underway, particularly concerning casualty figures and the nationalities and identities of victims. Fujairah Police also stressed complying with traffic regulations, observing speed limits and maintaining safe distances between vehicles, particularly when approaching congestion or slow-moving traffic. No verified fundraiser for the victims' families was reported in the sources reviewed for this article, so none is linked here; the Indian consulate's stated channel of support is its coordination with local authorities and the bereaved families it has already contacted.
